candidates: When a framework-specific Meta interface (e.g., `ReactMeta`, `VueMeta`, `AngularMeta`, `WebComponentsMeta`) extends the shared `Meta<T, MetaInput>` base type using two type parameters while the base only exposes one, add a `@ts-expect-error` suppression immediately before the `extends` clause. The comment must explain the specific reason (e.g., 'requires two type parameters to track both inferred renderer types and custom meta annotations, which Meta's single-parameter constraint does not support'), not a vague placeholder like 'hard'. All framework renderers should apply this pattern consistently.

File-level comments in test files that describe the overall testing approach (e.g., '// this file tests TypeScript types, so there are no assertions') must accurately reflect the file's actual content. If the file contains both type-level checks and runtime assertions (e.g., `expect(...).toBe(...)`), the comment must acknowledge both; do not claim there are no assertions when any `expect` calls are present.

Remove unused variables in test files. Story variables declared with `const` (e.g., `const Basic = meta.story(...)`) that are created solely to check TypeScript compilation but are never read afterward contribute dead code; either delete them or, if their declaration is the point of the test, add a comment explaining that.

When introducing a new renderer-specific `preview.ts` that references a framework type alias (e.g., `VueTypes`, `AngularTypes`), verify that the type is actually defined and exported from that renderer's `types.ts`. If no additional properties beyond the base renderer type are needed, reuse the existing renderer type (e.g., `VueRenderer`) rather than referencing an undefined alias that will produce a compilation error.

When implementing CSF factories for a new renderer (adding a `preview.ts` with `__definePreview` and framework-specific `Preview`, `Meta`, and `Story` interfaces), include a corresponding `csf-factories.test.ts` that mirrors the React renderer's test coverage: args split across meta and story, type errors for missing required args, decorator arg widening, story composition/extension via `extend`, and any renderer-specific patterns (e.g., Vue3 slots, Angular signals).

When setting a modification flag (e.g., `useCsfFactory: true`) on a sandbox template in `sandbox-templates.ts`, apply the same flag to all builder variants of the same renderer. If the Vite template for a renderer has a flag enabled, the corresponding RsBuild template must also have it unless there is a documented technical reason they must differ.

Ensure every `it(...)` and `test(...)` call within a test file has a unique, descriptive name. When two tests cover distinct scenarios within the same component category (e.g., plain class components vs. signal-based components, simple render vs. args-driven render), give each a name that unambiguously identifies the differentiating behavior.

When a function block computes a file-system path using a conditional (e.g., checking for `src/stories` to choose between `../src/stories/…` and `../stories/…`), any closely related paths derived from the same base directory should use the same conditional rather than being hardcoded to one branch. If a particular path is intentionally pinned to a single branch, add an inline comment explaining why the conditional does not apply to it.
